models.title: Unit labor cost from hourly compensation and productivity
models.summary: Hourly compensation divided by hourly labor productivity gives labor cost per output unit.

relationship.original_equation: Unit labor cost=nominal wage per hour / output per hour
relationship.locator: Learning Module3, Change in Nominal Wages, printed pp157-158 and p160 (PDF pp169-170,172), Examples8-9 and adjacent unit-labor-cost discussion
relationship.translation_notes: Compensation/service divided by output/service yields compensation/output. AVC=w/AP from LM1 applies only if labor exhausts variable costs; this separately defined unit-labor quantity does not impose that restriction.

models.title: Two-factor potential-output growth accounting
models.summary: Potential-output growth is decomposed into TFP growth and factor-income-share-weighted labor and capital growth.

relationship.original_equation: Growth in potentialGDP=growth inTFP+W_L*growth inlabor+W_C*growth incapital
relationship.locator: Learning Module3, Growth Accounting Equation, printed p176 and p178 (PDF pp188,190), unnumbered growth-accounting and TFP-residual equations
relationship.translation_notes: Pure1 closes the two-factor share partition; all rates and shares are dimensionless. The residual gA=gY-labor_share*gL-(1-labor_share)*gK is an inverse, not a new record. The source per-capita form is actually per labor input unless population and labor grow identically; that distinction is preserved rather than equated silently.

assumptions: Source assumption: differentiable constant-returns production, diminishing individual-input marginal products, and no externalities in the basic model.
Source assumption: factor income shares represent output elasticities under the model; capital share equals1-labor share.
Application profile: use instantaneous/log growth consistently; simple discrete percentage growth is the source first-order approximation.
limitations: TFP is a residual, not pure observable technology; omitted inputs and measurement errors can contribute.
No factor estimation or time-varying-share integration is performed.

models.title: Aggregate real output per labor hour
models.summary: Aggregate labor productivity divides realGDP by the total actual hours worked in producing that output.

relationship.locator: Learning Module3, Measures of Sustainable Growth / Labor Productivity, printed p183 (PDF p195), unnumbered Labor productivity=RealGDP/Aggregate hours
relationship.translation_notes: This independently defined monetary aggregate differs from physical good quantity per input: heterogeneous goods are first aggregated in real output value.
